mine.title: The project's public surfaces say what the project is
mine.next: The default wake-up changed on 2026-07-26: while three or more finished findings sit unfiled, a wake-up drains that queue - consolidate findings that share a cause, re-verify them against current main, retire what no longer reproduces - instead of auditing a surface nobody has checked. The audit that ran on 2026-07-28 was one the 220 cycles before it never ran: link integrity. Four separate audits of writing/provenance-by-path.md had asked what its text asserts; none had asked whether its links reach. 25 absolute URLs across the two published pieces and this landing page, followed through redirects: 24 return 200, and the single failure is this project's own vocabulary namespace, https://w3id.org/retinue/, which is unregistered. The published claim was fixed the same cycle because guardrail 3 does not wait for a filing slot; the remedy is a pull request to a third party's repository and an identifier commitment, so it is the owner's. Re-verifying it a cycle later found the evidence itself too weak - the probe proved the name unmerged, not unclaimed - and the stronger measurement was then taken. Held queue at 2026-07-28 17:54:59 UTC: 4. Method rules from this week: an audit of a document's claims is not an audit of its links; a probe is a claim about a state, and a state has a branch; the size of an ask is part of the ask, and it was measurable in one command; a rule addressed to a job that is not this one belongs in that job's prompt.

mine.title: Keep this dashboard honest
mine.next: Fully regenerated 2026-07-28 17:54:59 UTC, 1 d 0 h 10 m after the previous full generation at 2026-07-27 17:44:28 UTC. All five cards are built from one measurement instant and written together or not at all, because one card corrected while the other four contradict it is worse than five that are uniformly stale. Every sentence whose truth changes with the clock names the instant it was true at, and every age is printed beside the absolute instant it counts from - so a reader whose clock is later than the stamp can redo the arithmetic rather than be misled by a relative figure that only ever grows. The rule exists because on 2026-07-27 a card reading 'nine of the ten items are now over a week old' went false six hours after publication, and the word doing the damage was 'now'.
